slot.brief: Pendulum taken to a place where g changes by a small percentage (or with small error in length); find percentage change in T using differentials.

stem: The length of a simple pendulum is increased by 0.2% and it is taken to a place where the acceleration due to gravity is 0.4% less. The percentage change in the time period of the pendulum is approximately:

verdicts.working: For small changes, ΔT/T ≈ ½(Δl/l − Δg/g) = ½(0.2% − (−0.4%)) = 0.3%.

working:
T = 2 pi sqrt(L / g). Differentiating, ΔT/T = (1/2)(ΔL/L) - (1/2)(Δg/g). Given ΔL/L = +0.002 and Δg/g = -0.004. Therefore ΔT/T = 0.001 - 0.5(-0.004) = 0.001 + 0.002 = 0.003 = 0.3% increase.

Independent check: For small changes, ΔT/T ≈ ½(Δl/l − Δg/g) = ½(0.2% − (−0.4%)) = 0.3%.
solution:
For a simple pendulum, $T=2\pi\sqrt{L/g}$, so $\dfrac{\Delta T}{T}\approx\dfrac12\left(\dfrac{\Delta L}{L}-\dfrac{\Delta g}{g}\right)$. 
$$\frac{\Delta T}{T}=\frac12\bigl(0.2\%-(-0.4\%)\bigr)=0.3\%$$
Thus, the time period increases by $0.3\%$.
